rows.question: Analyse Tata
What is ROCE and why does it matter?
rows.text:
Return on capital employed (ROCE) = EBIT ÷ (total assets − current liabilities).  
It shows how efficiently a business turns the long‑term money it has invested—both equity and debt—into operating profit. By focusing on this ratio, an owner‑mindset can see whether the company is generating honest cash earnings on the capital that truly supports the business, without being distorted by short‑term financing tricks. A consistently high ROCE indicates a durable moat and a management team that creates value without relying on heavy borrowing.

rows.question: What is the PEG ratio?
rows.text: PEG ratio = P/E ÷ (5-year EPS CAGR × 100). The P/E adjusted for how fast earnings have grown. Around 1 or below is the classic growth-at-a-reasonable-price reading; it relies on past growth continuing.
